'''Isaura Meza Gómez-Palacio''' (born 11 May 1942) is a Mexican microbiologist who specialises in eukaryotic cytoskeletal protein genes. A 1980 [[Guggenheim Fellow]], she worked as a professor and researcher at [[CINVESTAV]].

==Biography==
She was born on 11 May 1942 in Mexico City.<ref name="GF 1980" /> She obtained her licentiate in biology from the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] in 1964 and her master of science degree from [[CINVESTAV]] in 1967.<ref name="GF 1980" /> After spending a year as a research fellow at [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]] (1966-1967) and a year of study at [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] (1968–1969), she obtained her PhD in Zoology from [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1972;<ref name="GF 1980" /> her dissertation was titled ''Studies on the chemistry and structure of sea urchin microtubules''.<ref>{{Cite thesis |title=Studies on the chemistry and structure of sea urchin microtubules |publisher=University of California, Berkeley |url=https://search.library.berkeley.edu/discovery/fulldisplay?docid=alma991008989199706532&context=L&vid=01UCS_BER:UCB&lang=en&search_scope=DN_and_CI&adaptor=Local%20Search%20Engine&tab=Default_UCLibrarySearch&query=any,contains,Isaura%20Meza&offset=0 |OCLC=17929492 |year=1972}}</ref>

She worked at UCB as a research fellow and teaching assistant from 1969 until 1972, when she moved to the [[University of Geneva]] to become a postdoctoral fellow.<ref name="GF 1980" /> In 1974, she left Geneva and returned to CINVESTAV to become assistant professor of cell biology; she was promoted to associate professor in 1975,<ref name="GF 1980" /> before eventually being promoted to researcher emeritus.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Centro de Investigación y de Estudios Avanzados del Instituto Politécnico Nacional |url=https://cinvestav.mx/zacatenco/ie/comunicaciones/isaura-meza-g243mez-palacio |access-date=2025-05-26 |website=Cinvestav |language=es}}</ref>

She focuses on eukaryotic cytoskeletal protein genes.<ref name="Rodríguez">{{Cite journal |last=Rodríguez Flores |first=Xochitl Pilli |title=La mujer mexicana en la ciencia |url=https://www.academia.edu/9323077/La_mujer_mexicana_en_la_ciencia |journal=Boletín Aleación de la Red de Divulgadores de la Ciencia y la Cultura "José Antonio Alzate" |language=es |pages=6–7}}</ref> Her work group at UCB was among the first to describe the protein organization of the structures that enable sperm [[flagella]] to move for egg fertilization.<ref name="Servin 2000">{{Cite news |date=2000-09-11 |title=Isaura Meza Gómez-Palacio: El movimiento es vida |url=https://www.jornada.com.mx/2000/09/11/cien-galeria.html |access-date=2025-05-25 |work=La Jornada |language=es |archive-date=26 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126151758/https://www.jornada.com.mx/2000/09/11/cien-galeria.html |url-status=live }}</ref> In 1980, she was awarded a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] to study [[tubulin]] genetics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Isaura Meza |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/isaura-meza/ |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=Guggenheim Fellowships |archive-date=25 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250125151556/https://www.gf.org/fellows/isaura-meza/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="GF 1980">{{Cite book |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Reports_of_the_President_and_the_Treasur/4Q40AAAAIAAJ |title=Reports of the President and the Treasurer |publisher=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation |year=1980 |pages=125–126}}</ref> In 2017, she led a research team identifying [[BIRC3]] for breast cancer treatment.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-06-22 |title=Identifican gen relacionado con la resistencia a tratamientos de cáncer de mama |url=http://www.conacytprensa.mx/index.php/centros-conacyt/cinvestav/16462-identifican-gen-relacionado-con-la-resistencia-a-tratamientos-de-cancer-de-mama |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180309182716/http://www.conacytprensa.mx/index.php/centros-conacyt/cinvestav/16462-identifican-gen-relacionado-con-la-resistencia-a-tratamientos-de-cancer-de-mama |archive-date=2018-03-09 |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=CONACYT |language=es}}</ref>

She co-authored a popular science book named ''Máquinas vivientes'' ({{lit|Living machines}}).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dra. Isaura Meza |url=http://www.codigoradio.cultura.df.gob.mx/index.php/gente-como-uno/1755-dra-isaura-meza |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180309120408/http://www.codigoradio.cultura.df.gob.mx/index.php/gente-como-uno/1755-dra-isaura-meza |archive-date=2018-03-09 |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=www.codigoradio.cultura.df.gob.mx |language=es}}</ref>

Mirna Servín said that her work "laid the foundations for what later became a boom in molecular biology studies of these parasites".<ref name="Servin 2000" /> Xochitl Pilli Rodríguez Flores called her "a pioneer in the study of the amoeba cytoskeleton in our country [Mexico]".<ref name="Rodríguez" /> In 2013, she was awarded the {{ill|Omecíhuatl Medal|es|Medalla Omecíhuatl}}.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Medalla Omecíhuatl |url=https://semujeres.cdmx.gob.mx/medalla-omecihuatl/ediciones-anteriores |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=Secretaria de las Mujeres de la Ciudad de México |language=es |archive-date=16 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220316041047/https://semujeres.cdmx.gob.mx/medalla-omecihuatl/ediciones-anteriores |url-status=live }}</ref>
